Common Urgent Care Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

E/M level defaulted to 99213 on every visit regardless of MDM complexity.

PMEX codes from 2021 MDM criteria on every encounter, capturing 99214 and 99215 when the documentation supports it.

Work injury filed to group health insurance instead of the workers comp carrier.

PMEX implements WC identification at registration and routes all work-related injuries to the correct WC carrier.

Laceration repair code not submitted alongside the E/M visit, losing procedure revenue.

PMEX identifies every separately billable procedure and submits it alongside the E/M with modifier 25.

Occupational health visit coded as standard E/M, missing the correct Z-code and employer billing.

PMEX applies occupational health CPT codes and Z02 diagnosis codes to DOT physicals and pre-employment evaluations.

Teleurgent care visit submitted without modifier 95 or with wrong place of service code.

PMEX applies modifier 95 and the correct POS code on every urgent care telehealth visit.

Eligibility not verified before visit, generating post-service denials for inactive coverage.

PMEX verifies insurance eligibility in real time at registration before every patient encounter.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Urgent Care Billing

Urgent care centers lose 18 to 25 percent of revenue to E/M under-coding, workers comp routing errors, and procedure bundling mistakes.

PATTERN 01

E/M Under-Coded on Every Visit

All urgent care visits defaulted to 99213 ($110). Patients with prescription management, imaging review, and multi-problem encounters qualify for 99214 ($175). $65 per qualifying visit. In a 100-visit-per-day center with 40 percent qualifying: $2,600 daily in systematic revenue loss.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes every urgent care E/M from 2021 MDM criteria: number and complexity of problems, data reviewed, and risk of management. Level is selected from documentation on every encounter.

PATTERN 02

Workers Comp Injury Filed to Group Health

Employee presents with a work-related injury. Front desk registers to the group health card on file. Group health denies: workers compensation injury. WC carrier never billed. Revenue lost and the patient receives a confusing bill.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX implements workers compensation identification at registration, routing all WC injuries to the correct carrier with WC-specific claim forms and first report of injury documentation before any health insurance is billed.

PATTERN 03

Procedure Not Billed Alongside E/M Visit

Laceration repair performed during the urgent care visit. Only the E/M submitted. Modifier 25 not applied. Repair code (12001, $180) never billed. In a center with 15 daily procedures, this is $2,700 daily in unbilled procedure revenue.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews clinical documentation for every visit and identifies separately billable procedures. Procedure codes are submitted alongside the E/M with modifier 25 on every qualifying encounter.
